title: reduce-batcher-memory-fragmentation-and-compact-scheduler-io-path
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Background: The continuous batcher has accumulated an allocation pattern that fragments the arena/slab allocator during long-lived jobs; coupled with the current KV cache grow/shrink semantics this produces periodic latency spikes and elevated RSS on high-throughput tenants. Goal: reduce memory fragmentation and steady-state RSS by introducing a compacting path for batcher allocations, stabilize scheduler IO bursts by coalescing small writes/read completions, and add guardrails to KV cache resizing so compaction doesn't induce tail latency. Non-goals: full allocator rewrite, changing public SDKs, or altering model execution kernels. Acceptance criteria: 1) steady-state RSS reduction >= 18% under the synthetic perf benchmark (steady 2000 concurrent sessions); 2) P95 tail latency for short (<=128 token) requests does not regress by more than 3ms; 3) KV cache resizing no longer triggers full GC pauses longer than 30ms in the repro harness; 4) rollout plan validated in staging with canary (5%) and automatic rollback on latency regressions.
technical_approach: Phase A: introduce per-tenant mini-slab pools inside the batcher and prefer reuse for ephemeral token buffers; add a background compaction worker that coalesces free spans during low load windows. Phase B: change scheduler IO path to aggregate completion callbacks and flush them through a single event flush to reduce syscall bursts; introduce a small 'coalesce window' (configurable ms) to batch epoll/kqueue completions. Phase C: KV cache: switch from aggressive shrink-to-fit to a hysteresis-based shrink policy and add 'soft-reserve' pages to avoid thrash when load spikes. Implementation notes: keep flags behind runtime feature gates, expose two knobs in Console (compaction cadence, coalesce window) and add telemetry for compaction duration and freed bytes.
rollout_plan: 1) feature-branch PR with unit and integration tests; 2) internal perf job against benchmark-runtime/large-repro to validate RSS and P95; 3) deploy to staging with compaction disabled by default, enable for internal tenant group; 4) 5% canary on runtime-2025.03 with automated SLO checks (Grafana/Alertmanager); 5) progressive ramp to 100% over 72h if no regressions. Rollback: flip feature flag and revert coalesce window if P95 increases > 5% or errors > 0.5%.
monitoring_and_metrics: Grafana dashboards to add: batcher.rss.by_tenant, batcher.free_spans.count, compaction.duration.histogram, scheduler.io.coalesce_latency, kvcache.resize.events, kvcache.pause.duration. Alerts: compaction.duration > 200ms for 5m; scheduler.coalesce_window > configured and P95 latency spike; kvcache.pause.duration > 30ms. Dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/scheduler/latency
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: compaction can increase CPU and temporarily increase tail latency; mitigation: background compaction runs only under CPU headroom threshold and has a cooperative yield. Risk: scheduler coalesce window introduces small additional latency for low-QPS tenants; mitigation: make window tenant-configurable and default to 2ms; monitor per-tenant P95 and disable for latency-sensitive tiers.
acceptance_tests: 1) existing unit test suite passes; 2) repro harness (github.com/redwood-infra/benchmarks/runtime-large-repro) shows RSS delta and latency adherence; 3) staging e2e with canary traffic for 24h without increased error budget; 4) manual smoke: memory profiling (heaptrack/pprof) confirms reduced fragmentation.
comments: 2025-02-16 - Triage meeting notes: Prioritized by SRE after repeated RSS alerts on perf/cluster-9. Decision: Do a staged compaction rather than an allocator swap to reduce risk.
2025-02-20 - Design review: @Priya Desai suggested adding a per-tenant throttle for compaction to avoid cross-tenant interference; agreed to add soft-reserve pages for hot tenants.

2025-02-25 - Implementation started: branched runtime/feature/compact-batcher-765210. Initial unit tests added for mini-slab reuse. Local perf shows 12% RSS reduction on dev harness. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345
2025-02-28 - Code review feedback from @Lars H. - prefer explicit memory fence when handing off free spans to background worker. Addressed in PR, pushed update and added unit test for race windows.
2025-03-01 - Staging run (internal tenants): compaction cadence 10s, coalesce window 3ms. Observed P95 +1.8ms and RSS -22% for busy tenants. KV resize pause event rate dropped by ~65% in the harness.
2025-03-03 - SRE requested a dashboard for compaction.backpressure; created dashboard panel and a temporary alert. Plan to enable 5% canary on 2025-03-05 if no regressions.
